aguascalientes: Small central state named for its hot springs; famous for the San Marcos Fair
baja-california: Peninsula state on the US border; home to Tijuana and Mexicali
baja-california-sur: Southern half of a long peninsula; home to Cabo San Lucas and La Paz
campeche: Gulf coast state with a walled colonial port city and the Calakmul ruins
chiapas: Southernmost state, bordering Guatemala; home to the Maya ruins of Palenque
chihuahua: The largest state by area; shares its name with a tiny dog breed
coahuila: Northern border state across from Texas; capital Saltillo
colima: One of the smallest states, on the Pacific, with an active volcano of the same name
durango: Northwestern state where many Hollywood westerns were filmed
guanajuato: Central state with a colorful silver-mining capital and the city of León
guerrero: Pacific state home to Acapulco and the silver town of Taxco
hidalgo: Central state named after the priest who started the independence war; capital Pachuca
jalisco: Home of tequila and mariachi; capital Guadalajara
state-of-mexico: The most populous state, wrapping around the capital city; capital Toluca
michoacan: Western state where monarch butterflies spend the winter; capital Morelia
morelos: Small state just south of the capital; capital Cuernavaca, the "city of eternal spring"
nayarit: Pacific state with surf towns like Sayulita
oaxaca: Southern state famous for mole, mezcal and Monte Albán
puebla: Central state known for mole poblano and Talavera pottery; Cinco de Mayo battle site
queretaro: Central state with a UNESCO-listed colonial capital and a famous aqueduct
quintana-roo: Caribbean state home to Cancún, Tulum and Playa del Carmen
san-luis-potosi: Central state with the Huasteca waterfalls; named after a French king and a Bolivian mine
sinaloa: Pacific state with the beach city of Mazatlán; capital Culiacán
sonora: Desert border state across from Arizona; capital Hermosillo
tabasco: Gulf state of rivers and swamps; shares its name with a famous hot sauce
tamaulipas: Gulf state on the Texas border; cities include Reynosa and Matamoros
tlaxcala: The smallest state, completely surrounded by its neighbours east of the capital
veracruz: Long Gulf coast state with Mexico's oldest major port
yucatan: Peninsula state with Chichén Itzá and the capital Mérida
zacatecas: Silver-mining state with a pink-stone colonial capital
mexico-city: The federal capital, built on the old Aztec city of Tenochtitlan
